quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: I missed the train because my alarm didn't go off, so I had to take a taxi.
quests.textToSpeak: I missed the train because my alarm didn't go off, so I had to take a taxi.
options: Falls after 'train', 'off' and 'taxi'
Lifts after 'train' and 'off', fall on 'taxi'
quests.correctAnswer: Lifts after 'train' and 'off', fall on 'taxi'
quests.hint: There are three parts here. Ask which ones are completed thoughts and which ones lead into the next.
quests.explanation: The first two chunks lead into a reason and a result, so they lift. Only 'taxi' finishes the story and falls.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 In a chain of clauses, each link lifts and only the last one falls.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: We finally found the leak, and it was behind the fridge.
quests.textToSpeak: We finally found the leak, and it was behind the fridge.
options: Peak on 'leak' — the thing that was found
Peak on 'fridge' — the surprising location
quests.correctAnswer: Peak on 'fridge' — the surprising location
quests.hint: Everyone already knows something was being searched for. What is new?
quests.explanation: 'Leak' was the object of the search, so it is given. 'Fridge' is the surprise, so it takes the peak and the fall.
quests.pitchRule: 🎯 In a long sentence the surprising last detail takes the peak.

quests.instruction: You explain a delay to a customer.
quests.word: We found a problem with the supplier, so we had to rebuild the order.
quests.textToSpeak: We found a problem with the supplier, so we had to rebuild the order.
options: Lift after 'supplier', fall on 'order'
Fall after 'supplier', fall on 'order'
quests.correctAnswer: Lift after 'supplier', fall on 'order'
quests.hint: The second clause is the consequence of the first. Where does the voice wait?
quests.explanation: The problem is only the cause, so it lifts. The consequence is the main news and falls.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 Cause lifts, consequence falls.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: The students who studied passed.
quests.textToSpeak: The students who studied passed.
options: Pauses around 'who studied' — all passed, and they studied
No pause — all who studied passed
quests.correctAnswer: No pause — all who studied passed
quests.hint: Decide whether the speaker is separating the students into groups or adding a comment about all of them.
quests.explanation: Without pauses, 'who studied' defines which students passed. With pauses and lifts, it becomes extra information about all of them.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️ Pauses turn a defining phrase into a side comment.

quests.instruction: A colleague describes an employee she will introduce.
quests.word: I'll introduce you to the designer, who's just joined.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll introduce you to the designer, who's just joined.
options: Lift on 'designer', fall on 'joined' — extra information
No lift on 'designer' — identifies which designer
quests.correctAnswer: Lift on 'designer', fall on 'joined' — extra information
quests.hint: This time, ask whether 'who's just joined' tells you which designer or simply adds a fact.
quests.explanation: A lift after 'designer' marks the clause as extra information. Without it, the clause would tell you which designer.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 A lifted noun followed by a clause signals extra information.

quests.instruction: A manager checks the guest list and wants to be sure interns aren't forgotten.
quests.word: Everyone's invited, interns included.
quests.textToSpeak: Everyone's invited, interns included.
options: Peak on 'invited' — confirming the invitation
Peak on 'interns' — making sure they're not forgotten
quests.correctAnswer: Peak on 'interns' — making sure they're not forgotten
quests.hint: The invitation itself isn't in doubt. Who might have been left out?
quests.explanation: 'Interns included' adds a group that might be missed, so 'interns' takes the peak. 'Invited' is already agreed.
quests.pitchRule: 🎯 A final 'included' phrase peaks on the group being added.

quests.instruction: You begin a decision aloud, with more to come.
quests.word: If the test comes back negative,
quests.textToSpeak: If the test comes back negative,
options: Fall on 'negative' — thought finished
Lift on 'negative' — result still to come
quests.correctAnswer: Lift on 'negative' — result still to come
quests.hint: There is no result yet. Which ending leaves the listener waiting?
quests.explanation: A lift keeps the condition open until the result arrives. A fall would end the sentence too early.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️ A condition needs a lift because the result is missing.

quests.instruction: Someone is telling a story and pauses mid-sentence.
quests.word: And as soon as she walked in,
quests.textToSpeak: And as soon as she walked in,
options: Fall on 'in' — story ends
Lift on 'in' — story continues
quests.correctAnswer: Lift on 'in' — story continues
quests.hint: The story is not finished. Notice how the speaker's voice waits.
quests.explanation: A lift on 'in' tells listeners that more is coming, and it builds suspense. A fall would sound like an incomplete story that had ended.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️ A lift holds the floor and builds anticipation.

quests.instruction: Now you complete the sentence and end the thought.
quests.word: Then we can finally start the second phase.
quests.textToSpeak: Then we can finally start the second phase.
options: Fall on 'phase' — thought complete
Lift on 'phase' — continues
quests.correctAnswer: Fall on 'phase' — thought complete
quests.hint: The second half of a sentence is delivered. Ask whether the speaker is done.
quests.explanation: This clause finishes the idea, so it falls on 'phase'. A lift would keep the listener waiting for more.
quests.pitchRule: 📉 The final clause of a plan closes with a fall.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: Some people prefer working alone, while others thrive in teams.
quests.textToSpeak: Some people prefer working alone, while others thrive in teams.
options: Lift on 'alone', fall on 'teams'
Fall on 'alone', fall on 'teams'
quests.correctAnswer: Lift on 'alone', fall on 'teams'
quests.hint: Two groups of people are compared. Listen to how the first half hands over.
quests.explanation: The first half lifts because the contrast is coming, and the second half falls to complete the comparison.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 A comparison lifts on the first half and falls on the second.

quests.instruction: A colleague is hurt by feedback, and you want to soften it.
quests.word: It's a solid draft, it just needs a stronger ending.
quests.textToSpeak: It's a solid draft, it just needs a stronger ending.
options: Quick, flat fall on 'ending' — dismissive feedback
Slower pace on 'stronger ending', warm fall — softened feedback
quests.correctAnswer: Slower pace on 'stronger ending', warm fall — softened feedback
quests.hint: The criticism is real but the speaker cares. Listen to how the pace changes.
quests.explanation: A slower, warmer second half signals care while delivering the criticism. A quick, flat ending would sound dismissive.
quests.pitchRule: 🤝 Warm pacing softens a criticism.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: He's brilliant with clients, and, frankly, terrible with deadlines.
quests.textToSpeak: He's brilliant with clients, and, frankly, terrible with deadlines.
options: Pause before 'frankly', peak on 'terrible' — candid contrast
No pause, even stress — neutral description
quests.correctAnswer: Pause before 'frankly', peak on 'terrible' — candid contrast
quests.hint: A single word in the middle changes the tone. Where does the speaker pause?
quests.explanation: A short pause before 'frankly' prepares the listener for a blunt remark, and the peak on 'terrible' delivers it. An even delivery would hide the contrast.
quests.pitchRule: 🎯 A pause plus a peak turns a remark into candour.

quests.instruction: Your manager states two facts and stresses the important one.
quests.word: The report is due on Friday, and the client wants it in PDF.
quests.textToSpeak: The report is due on Friday, and the client wants it in PDF.
options: Peak on 'PDF' — the new requirement
Peak on 'Friday' — the deadline
quests.correctAnswer: Peak on 'PDF' — the new requirement
quests.hint: The first fact is already known to everyone. What is the new information?
quests.explanation: The deadline was already agreed, so it stays lower. The format is new, so 'PDF' takes the peak and the fall.
quests.pitchRule: 🎯 The new requirement gets the peak; the known one stays low.

quests.instruction: You have already told your friend about the party, and now you add a detail.
quests.word: The party is on Saturday, but it starts at noon.
quests.textToSpeak: The party is on Saturday, but it starts at noon.
options: Peak on 'party' — the topic
Peak on 'noon' — the surprising time
quests.correctAnswer: Peak on 'noon' — the surprising time
quests.hint: Your friend knows about the party. What is new?
quests.explanation: 'Party' and 'Saturday' are given, so they are lower. 'Noon' is the surprising new detail, so it takes the peak.
quests.pitchRule: 🎯 The unexpected detail deserves the strongest peak.

quests.instruction: You correct a misunderstanding in a group email.
quests.word: The budget was approved last month, not this month.
quests.textToSpeak: The budget was approved last month, not this month.
options: Peaks on 'last' and 'this' — the corrected time
Peak on 'approved' — the action being corrected
quests.correctAnswer: Peaks on 'last' and 'this' — the corrected time
quests.hint: The action isn't in dispute. Which words show the real difference?
quests.explanation: The confusion is about when, so 'last' and 'this' carry the peaks. 'Approved' is shared knowledge.
quests.pitchRule: 🎯 Corrections in long sentences place peaks on the contrasted words.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: I told her, as gently as I could, that the job was gone.
quests.textToSpeak: I told her, as gently as I could, that the job was gone.
options: Falls at both edges of 'as gently as I could'
Lifts at both edges of 'as gently as I could'
quests.correctAnswer: Lifts at both edges of 'as gently as I could'
quests.hint: The middle of the sentence is a comment on how something was said. How does the voice enter and leave it?
quests.explanation: The comment is a side note, so it sits between lifts and is spoken lower. The main clause resumes and falls on 'gone'.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 A side comment is bracketed by lifts.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: My neighbor, whom I've never actually met, left a note on my door.
quests.textToSpeak: My neighbor, whom I've never actually met, left a note on my door.
options: Lifts at both edges of 'whom I've never actually met'
Falls at both edges of 'whom I've never actually met'
quests.correctAnswer: Lifts at both edges of 'whom I've never actually met'
quests.hint: There is a long extra piece inside the sentence. Listen to the return to the main line.
quests.explanation: The interruption is a background remark, so it is framed by lifts. After it, the main clause continues and falls on 'door'.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 Extra information is folded inside the main sentence with lifts.

quests.instruction: You quote what your manager promised.
quests.word: She said, and I quote, that nobody would lose their job.
quests.textToSpeak: She said, and I quote, that nobody would lose their job.
options: Lifts at both edges of 'and I quote'
Falls at both edges of 'and I quote'
quests.correctAnswer: Lifts at both edges of 'and I quote'
quests.hint: The middle phrase draws attention to what follows. Which pattern signals it?
quests.explanation: 'And I quote' is a short parenthesis, so it lifts on both sides. The sentence falls on 'job'.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 A parenthesis inside a sentence is lifted and lowered in volume.

quests.instruction: You explain the plan for fixing a bug.
quests.word: First we'll check the data, then we'll fix the errors, and finally we'll rerun the test.
quests.textToSpeak: First we'll check the data, then we'll fix the errors, and finally we'll rerun the test.
options: Lift on 'data' and 'errors', fall on 'test'
Fall on 'data', 'errors' and 'test'
quests.correctAnswer: Lift on 'data' and 'errors', fall on 'test'
quests.hint: Three steps are planned in order. Which steps are still open?
quests.explanation: Steps lift until the last one, so the listener knows how many steps remain. The last falls to say it's the last.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 Long instructions lift through the middle steps.

quests.instruction: A friend asks whether your commute is bad, and you are worn down by it.
quests.word: Forty minutes on a packed train, then a ten-minute walk in the rain.
quests.textToSpeak: Forty minutes on a packed train, then a ten-minute walk in the rain.
options: Quick, light delivery with a high final fall — cheerful
Heavy, slowing delivery with a low final fall — exasperated
quests.correctAnswer: Heavy, slowing delivery with a low final fall — exasperated
quests.hint: The sentence is a list of facts, but the situation tells you the mood. How fast does the speaker sound?
quests.explanation: A slow, heavy delivery with a low fall shows that the commute wears the speaker down. A light, quick one would sound cheerful.
quests.pitchRule: 😮‍💨 Exasperation slows the pace and lowers the fall.

quests.instruction: A facilitator is trying to calm a workshop that has started to panic.
quests.word: Right, let's take this one step at a time.
quests.textToSpeak: Right, let's take this one step at a time.
options: Fast pace, high start, sharp fall — urgent
Slow, even pace, gentle fall — calming
quests.correctAnswer: Slow, even pace, gentle fall — calming
quests.hint: The group is anxious. What kind of pace would help them?
quests.explanation: A slow, even pace and a gentle fall on 'time' calm the room. A faster, higher delivery would add urgency.
quests.pitchRule: 💛 A slow, even pace is how a calming voice sounds.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: Even though it was raining, we decided to go, and we're glad we did.
quests.textToSpeak: Even though it was raining, we decided to go, and we're glad we did.
options: Lifts after 'raining' and 'go', fall on 'did'
Falls after 'raining', 'go' and 'did'
quests.correctAnswer: Lifts after 'raining' and 'go', fall on 'did'
quests.hint: The sentence has three parts. Which ones lead into the next?
quests.explanation: The clauses connect a surprise, a decision, and a result. Lifts join them and the last fall lands the conclusion.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 A story with a happy ending lifts until the end.

quests.instruction: A client reluctantly accepts a poor delivery.
quests.word: Well, it does the job, I suppose, even if it isn't pretty.
quests.textToSpeak: Well, it does the job, I suppose, even if it isn't pretty.
options: Level, slowing fall on 'pretty' — reluctant acceptance
Bright lift on 'job' — pleased approval
quests.correctAnswer: Level, slowing fall on 'pretty' — reluctant acceptance
quests.hint: The phrase 'I suppose' is a clue. Does the voice sound pleased?
quests.explanation: A level, slowing ending shows that the client is putting up with it. A bright lift would sound pleased.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 Reluctant acceptance fades at the end.

quests.instruction: You reframe a lost bid for your team.
quests.word: We lost the bid, but honestly, I think we learned more than we would have by winning.
quests.textToSpeak: We lost the bid, but honestly, I think we learned more than we would have by winning.
options: Peak on 'learned' — the positive reframe
Peak on 'lost' — the failure being stressed
quests.correctAnswer: Peak on 'learned' — the positive reframe
quests.hint: The speaker wants the team encouraged. Which word carries that?
quests.explanation: The reframing is the 'learned', so it takes the peak. 'Lost' is acknowledged but not emphasized.
quests.pitchRule: 🎯 Reframing places the peak on the benefit, not the loss.

quests.instruction: You ask a colleague about a favor that depends on timing.
quests.word: If I sent you the file tonight, could you look at it before the meeting?
quests.textToSpeak: If I sent you the file tonight, could you look at it before the meeting?
options: Fall on 'tonight', fall on 'meeting'
Small lift on 'tonight', final rise on 'meeting'
quests.correctAnswer: Small lift on 'tonight', final rise on 'meeting'
quests.hint: There's a conditional part and a request. Which part has the final rise?
quests.explanation: The 'if' clause lifts a little because the question follows. The final rise on 'meeting' completes the yes/no request.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📈 The setup lifts slightly, and the question rises at the end.

quests.instruction: You ask a manager for advice on a hard situation.
quests.word: What would you do if the client refused to pay?
quests.textToSpeak: What would you do if the client refused to pay?
options: Fall on 'pay' — WH-question with a hypothetical
Rise on 'pay' — yes/no question about the client
quests.correctAnswer: Fall on 'pay' — WH-question with a hypothetical
quests.hint: The question has a WH-word at the start. Listen to how the hypothetical part ends.
quests.explanation: Even with an 'if' clause, the question remains a WH-question, so it falls on 'pay'. The manager is expected to give a full answer.
quests.pitchRule: 📉 A WH-question keeps its fall even with a hypothetical clause.

quests.instruction: Heavy rain has ruined the plan for a picnic, and a friend rings you.
quests.word: Since it's raining, where should we go instead?
quests.textToSpeak: Since it's raining, where should we go instead?
options: Lift on 'raining', fall on 'instead' — setup, then WH-question
Fall on 'raining', rise on 'instead' — setup, then yes/no
quests.correctAnswer: Lift on 'raining', fall on 'instead' — setup, then WH-question
quests.hint: There is a reason and a question. Which part cannot end the sentence?
quests.explanation: The reason sets up the question, so it lifts. The WH-question asks for a place and falls on 'instead'.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 A reason lifts into a WH-question that falls.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: When I got to the airport, I realized my passport was still at home, which meant I had to turn back.
quests.textToSpeak: When I got to the airport, I realized my passport was still at home, which meant I had to turn back.
options: Falls after 'airport', 'home' and 'back'
Lifts after 'airport' and 'home', fall on 'back'
quests.correctAnswer: Lifts after 'airport' and 'home', fall on 'back'
quests.hint: Recall how stories are built from clauses. Which clause lifts into the next?
quests.explanation: Each clause introduces the next event, so the first two lift. The last clause resolves and falls.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 A story chain uses lifts for each turning point and a fall for the end.

quests.instruction: A colleague says to guess and see, but you want to settle the timing, not the method.
quests.word: I'd rather ask now than guess later.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd rather ask now than guess later.
options: Peaks on 'ask' and 'guess' — contrasted actions
Peaks on 'now' and 'later' — contrasted timing
quests.correctAnswer: Peaks on 'now' and 'later' — contrasted timing
quests.hint: The situation tells you what you are contesting. Which two words are the alternatives?
quests.explanation: You aren't disputing asking versus guessing, only when. So 'now' and 'later' carry the peaks.
quests.pitchRule: 🎯 Context decides which pair of words is contrasted.

quests.instruction: You correct a date and continue with more information.
quests.word: The launch isn't in March, it's in May, and the press release goes out a week before.
quests.textToSpeak: The launch isn't in March, it's in May, and the press release goes out a week before.
options: Fall on 'March', 'May' and 'before' with no contrast
Peaks on 'March' and 'May', lift on 'May', fall on 'before'
quests.correctAnswer: Peaks on 'March' and 'May', lift on 'May', fall on 'before'
quests.hint: There are three pieces: a denial, a correction and an addition. Track which words carry the most pitch.
quests.explanation: The two months are contrasted, so they carry peaks. The correction lifts because an addition follows, and 'before' closes with a fall.
quests.pitchRule: 🎯↗️📉 Focus words carry peaks, clauses lift, and the last falls.
